section.title: Resources Tree
section.para: The Resources tree displays GMAT resources and organizes them into logical groups and represents any objects that might be used or called in the Mission tree. This tree allows a user to add, edit, rename, or delete most available resources. The Resources tree can be edited either in the GMAT GUI or by loading or syncing a script file. All objects created in a GMAT script using a Create command are found in the Resources tree in the GMAT desktop. The default Resource tree is displayed below ().

section.title: Organization
section.para: The Resources tree displays created resources organized into folders by object category. The SolarSystem and Solvers folders contain more specific folders which can be found by clicking the expand (+) icon. Conversely, folders can be collapsed by clicking the minimize (-) icon.

section.title: Folder Menus
section.para: Resources can be added by right clicking the folder of the resource and clicking the resource type from the available menu. Most folders have only one available resource type; for example if the Spacecraft folder is right-clicked, the user can only click “Add Spacecraft” (). Other folders have multiple objects that can be added and the user must first select the “Add” menu before selecting the object; for example to add a ChemicalTank, right click the “Hardware” folder, select “Add”, then the list of available resource types is displayed and the user can click “Fuel Tank” (). User-defined solar system resources are added by right-clicking either Sun or a default CelestialBody resource. By right-clicking Sun the user can add a Planet, Comet, or Asteroid to the solar system. By right-clicking a Planet the user can add a Moon to that Planet.

section.title: Resource Menus
section.para: Resources can be edited by right-clicking on the resources and selecting one of the options from the menu ().

To open a resource, you can either right-click the resource and select “Open”, or you can double click the resource. Conversely, the resource can be closed either by options in the resource properties window or selecting “Close” from the resource menu. When a resource is opened and the name is right-clicked in the Resource tree, the only options in the object menu are “Open” and “Close”.

Once a resource has been created, the user can rename it to any valid name. Valid names must begin with a letter and may be followed by any combination of letters digits and underscores. Invalid names include:
Folder names (eg, Spacecraft)
Command names (eg, Propagate)
Names already in use (eg, naming two variables “var”)
Keywords (eg, “GMAT” or “function”)
Names with spaces

Resources can be deleted by right clicking the object and selecting “Delete”. Resources cannot be deleted if they are used by another resource or command and an error with be thrown. For example, a Spacecraft resource cannot be deleted if one of its properties (eg. DefaultSC.A1ModJulian) is being used by the Report command. Some default objects cannot be deleted. In such cases, the Delete menu item will not be shown. They include:
Default coordinate systems
EarthMJ2000Eq
EarthMJ2000Ec
EarthFixed
EarthICRF
Default planetary bodies
Sun
Mercury
Venus
Earth
Luna
Mars
Jupiter
Saturn
Uranus
Neptune
Pluto

Objects can be cloned by selecting the “Clone” option in the menu. A cloned object will be an exact copy of the original object with a different name. Some objects cannot be cloned. In such cases, the Clone menu item will not be available. The only objects that cannot be cloned are:
Default coordinate systems (listed above)
Default planetary bodies (listed above)
Propagator resource objects

Qt also provides an explicit Clone propagator command in the Edit menu and on a named propagator's context menu. This additional command supports copying propagators while retaining the standard Clone restrictions above. Choose the copy's name and settings in the same resource-copy editor, then select Clone to commit them together. Cancel discards the pending copy.

Copy coordinate system in the Edit menu and a default coordinate system's context menu creates an editable, user-defined coordinate system from that frame. The copy starts with the original's origin, axes type and writable axes settings. Choose a new name and apply any desired changes in the copy editor. The original default frame remains protected. This additional command also accepts user-defined coordinate systems; the standard Clone command retains the restrictions above.

Copy celestial body in the Edit menu and a default body's context menu creates a named copy of a default planet, moon or the Sun. The copy retains its PhysicalBody identity, native ephemeris and orientation model, physical values and appearance. The copy editor offers the body's supported settings and shows its physical model. Copy commits the name and settings together; Cancel discards the draft. The original default body remains protected.

The body copy writes its physical identity before dependent settings. It retains un-authored effective values and uses full native numeric precision. Authored scalar expressions keep their source form. Kernel and directory lists copy their effective contents in their existing order. This preserves the configured list when the original source used additive or indexed assignments. The same command accepts user-defined bodies, including another physical-body copy.

The built-in SolarSystemBarycenter can be cloned into a named, user-defined barycenter. The copy retains EphemerisSource = SolarSystemBarycenter, so its state, velocity, acceleration and mass use the original native ephemeris point. It does not become a mass-weighted approximation using a list of planets. Copy calculated point in the Edit menu and the built-in point's context menu opens the same copy editor. This command also accepts user-defined calculated points. The original built-in point remains protected.

The copy keeps the original's output filenames and function paths, including values supplied by defaults rather than written explicitly in the script. Authored settings and expressions retain their source form. Choose another output filename in the copy's settings when separate output files are wanted. Cloning a resource copies its configuration; it does not copy the external data or function files.
When an array's formula grid refers to that same array, the clone's formulas use the new array's name. References to other arrays and resource properties retain their original names.

The copy retains authored integrator or ephemeris settings and references to other resources. A numerical propagator's effective force-model reference is retained even when the original source used an implicit model. The command copies the propagator setup; it does not create a separate Resource Tree object for its owned integrator or duplicate its configured force-model resource.

Resources declared or configured in included files can be cloned after a successful Build. The copy's declaration and settings are added to the current script; the included files remain unchanged. The copy uses the settings read by that Build, including nested includes and subsequent configuration assignments in the current script. Rebuild after editing an included file to use its updated settings.

If the mission starts in an included file that also configures resources, move the mission boundary into the current script before cloning. This preserves the order in which configuration expressions use other resources. Arrays whose marked mission initializer is in an included file must still be cloned in their defining script.
